claims.explanation: JZL-184 inhibits monoacylglycerol lipase (MGLL/MAGL), the enzyme that degrades 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG); MAGL is overexpressed in aggressive tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma where it supplies free fatty acids for lipid signaling and energy, so lines with high MGLL expression and active endocannabinoid/lipid metabolism are expected to be most dependent on MAGL and thus selectively killed. Sensitivity is further shaped by downstream lipid-signaling and proliferation pathways (PI3K/AKT/MTOR, KRAS/MAPK, PTEN loss), which determine whether loss of MAGL-derived lipid precursors impairs viability. Lines with low MGLL expression or intact alternative lipid sources are relatively protected.

features.basis: MAGL is the drug target and is overexpressed in aggressive tumors, so high expression predicts dependence and killing (PMID 27767105)
PI3K pathway activation is enriched in killed lines and may increase dependence on MAGL-derived lipid signaling
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and is enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with lipid-dependent survival
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among killed lines, linking MAPK-driven lipid metabolism to MAGL dependence
BRAF mutations appear in several sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven lipid dependency
ARID1A mutations are frequent in killed lines, possibly reflecting chromatin-state dependence on lipid signaling
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, consistent with altered stress/lipid metabolism
MTOR pathway mutations in sensitive lines suggest dependence on lipid-fueled mTOR signaling
STK11/LKB1 mutations are enriched in least-affected lines, possibly indicating metabolic rewiring that bypasses MAGL dependence
NF1 mutations appear in several resistant lines, suggesting RAS/MAPK activation alone is insufficient without lipid dependency
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines, possibly reflecting cell-cycle-independent survival
EGFR mutations appear in resistant lines, suggesting alternative growth-factor signaling sustains viability
